input.quote: at least eighteen (18) months prior to the expiration of the Term, M&I shall submit to Customer a written proposal for renewal of this Agreement. Customer will respond to such proposal within six (6) months following receipt and inform M&I in writing whether or not Customer desires to renew this Agreement. If M&I and Customer are unable to agree upon the terms for renewal of this Agreement at least six (6) months prior to the expiration of the Term, then Customer may, at its option, renew this Agreement for one (1) twelve month period at the then-current terms and conditions of this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no automatic renewal. Section 2.1 provides a fixed initial Term "unless extended or earlier terminated," and Section 2.2 makes any renewal dependent on M&I's written proposal and Customer's written agreement to renewal terms — renewal only by mutual written agreement, which meets the preferred position. Because renewal is never automatic, the conditional preferred elements (12-month renewal term, 30-day Customer opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) and the price-uplift caps are not engaged: there is no unilateral Vendor uplift mechanic and no non-renewal notice window is imposed on Customer at all (silence simply lets the Term expire). The only unilateral extension right runs in our favour — Customer may elect a single twelve-month extension "at the then-current terms and conditions," i.e. with no price increase. The 18-month M&I proposal lead time and the 5-month deadline for exercising Customer's option are noted but are not non-renewal notice windows and benefit Customer, so no redline is proposed.
